metrics.definition: Total parcel cost divided by shipped orders. Orders that shipped nothing are excluded from both numerator and denominator.
metrics.version_history: 1.0 (2026-08-08) certified with not-shipped orders excluded, stated on the page next to the number.
metrics.tier_reason: An order with no parcel has no parcel cost. Including it would divide real cost across unreal volume and quietly flatter the figure.

metrics.definition: Mean elapsed hours between goods being received and being available to pick.
metrics.tier_reason: Stock that has arrived but is not put away cannot fill an order, so this sits upstream of every fill rate on the register.

metrics.definition: End-of-month inventory valued at cost, divided by that month's sales at retail. Valuation follows the Census Monthly Retail Trade Survey so the figure means the same thing as the anchor.
metrics.tier_reason: The only metric here checked directly against a real published series. It sits below the Census sector band by design, because this is a fulfillment network and the sector figure includes store selling floors.

metrics.definition: Order lines whose ship date fell on or before the promise date, divided by lines that shipped at all.
metrics.tier_reason: An unshipped line is a fill failure, not a lateness failure. Counting it in both would charge one miss to two metrics, which is exactly the double-counting this module exists to surface.

metrics.definition: Orders in which every line shipped its full ordered quantity, divided by all orders placed in the period, including orders that shipped nothing.
metrics.version_history: 1.0 (2026-08-08) certified at first publication. Chosen over line and unit fill because it is the only one of the three that matches what the customer experiences.
metrics.tier_reason: A customer whose three-line order arrives missing a line did not receive 67% of an order; they received an incomplete order. Order fill is the only definition that says so.

metrics.definition: Actual parcel cost minus what the same shipped units would have cost in a single parcel from the primary node.
metrics.version_history: 1.0 (2026-08-08) certified on the incremental definition after the average-versus-average comparison was rejected.
metrics.tier_reason: Split orders are systematically larger baskets. Comparing the average cost of split orders against the average cost of single-node orders compares two different populations and flatters the split.

metrics.definition: Orders whose shipped units came from more than one fulfillment node, divided by all orders. Node count, not parcel count.
metrics.version_history: 1.0 (2026-08-08) certified on the by-node definition. The by-parcel definition is retained as exploratory; see classification_rules.md.
metrics.tier_reason: Node count responds to the allocation decision under review. Parcel count also responds to carton sizing and packaging rules, which are a different problem with a different owner.

metrics.definition: Units processed divided by paid labor hours, by function.
metrics.tier_reason: Costed at BLS Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics medians for the Seattle-Tacoma-Bellevue metro, May 2025, so cost per order is a real regional number rather than an invented rate.

metrics.definition: Best units any single node could have shipped for each order, divided by units ordered.
metrics.tier_reason: A modelled alternative history, not a measurement. It prices the governance decision and must never be reported as achieved service.

metrics.definition: Order lines that shipped their full ordered quantity, divided by all order lines.
metrics.version_history: 1.0 (2026-08-08) retained as exploratory at first publication. Deliberately not retired.
metrics.tier_reason: Useful as an assortment-coverage diagnostic, and it is what the merchant team has always read. Retaining it and labelling it is the governance act; quietly deleting it would move the disagreement rather than resolve it.

metrics.definition: Units shipped divided by units ordered.
metrics.version_history: 1.0 (2026-08-08) retained as exploratory at first publication.
metrics.tier_reason: The most forgiving of the three and therefore the one most often quoted upward. Retained as a depth-of-stock diagnostic, explicitly not as the service number.
